title: Ensemble hub: hub.yaml
description: A hub, in ~/.config/ensemble/hub/hub.yaml: it provides services and connects runners, and has no helper team. Always a server (`ensemble-hub serve`): accounts with roles, a knowledge vault and the models that distill it, and the issues of a tracker handed to the runners of the people they are assigned to. Nothing has a default value: every setting is written, except what may be left out because leaving it out means 'not used' (`tasks`, and a backend's `api_key_env`).

owner.description: The hub's name, such as the organization or the person who runs it.

llm_backends.description: Model endpoints the hub itself uses, such as for distilling knowledge. The key is the backend's name. Separate from the helper team's, which a company may share. `{}` when there are none.

knowledge.description: The knowledge vault, and how shares become notes.

tasks.description: The task inbox: issues in a tracker, with the label, go to the runners of the accounts they are assigned to, and their progress, questions and results are written back. Leave it out for no inbox.

server.description: Where `ensemble-hub serve` listens for runners and the REST API, and how people join.

roles.description: The hub's roles, named as you like, each a list of what its users may do. Users and their tokens are kept in database.db beside this file, not here: `ensemble-hub user add NAME --role R`.

interfaces.description: How it is reached: each interface it turns on. Left out, the command line alone is on; it must be on.

cli.description: `ensemble-hub …` on its computer, run by the running process over its socket when it runs.

mcp.description: MCP over HTTP at `/mcp` on the hub's port, for client agents, signed in with an account's token as the API key: share, recall and tasks. Left out: no MCP.

url.description: The address clients reach the hub at, such as https://hub.example.com, with no path: a new token's answer tells them to add `<url>/mcp` to their agent.

listen.description: The address and port to listen on, for runners (WebSocket), the REST API and MCP under /api/v1/. Put a TLS reverse proxy such as Caddy in front for the internet, or listen on a LAN or VPN address.

registration.description: How people join. `type` decides which other settings there are.

hours.description: How long a login (POST /api/v1/login) lasts before its session token stops working.

failures.description: Failed logins for one name before it is refused for a while.

minutes.description: How long a name is refused after too many failed logins.

type.description: approval: anyone who reaches the hub may sign up (POST /api/v1/register) and gets a token at once; it works once an admin approves the sign-up and gives a role.

max_pending.description: Most sign-ups waiting for approval at once; more are refused until an admin handles some.

type.description: closed: nobody signs up; an admin adds users.

permission.description: share: keep knowledge in the organization vault. recall: read its notes. tasks: receive the tasks the hub's inbox finds assigned to you. admin: manage users, approve sign-ups, give roles, revoke tokens. compute: use other people's shared runners, the agents and models they offer. host: connect a shared runner, which works for those whose role has compute.

tracker.description: Where the issues are kept. `type` decides which other settings there are.

label.description: The signal: an issue with this label is for the helper teams of the person it is assigned to. A second label `<label>:<team>/<agent>` gives it to that agent; without one it goes to the backlog.

poll_seconds.description: Seconds between two looks at the tracker.

type.description: local_markdown: a folder of `<id>.md` issues, each with title, assignee, labels, project and status in its front matter. People write them; Ensemble changes only `status` and appends comments.

dir.description: The folder, relative to the hub's directory or absolute. Often a git repository a team shares.

vault.description: The vault's directory, a git repository, relative to the hub's directory or absolute. `ensemble-hub init` makes it.

try.description: The models that turn shares into notes, in order. Each share uses the first whose backend answers and serves it; with one model, it is simply used. The model gets no tools: text in, text out.

when_none.description: What happens when none of the models in `try` can be used. fail: the share goes to review/, saying what each backend answered. wait: the share waits and is tried again later.

max_chars.description: Most characters one recall returns, all notes together.

embed.description: An embedding model, so notes are found by what they mean as well as by their words. Left out: by their words alone.

backend.description: One of llm_backends, of type openai-compatible-api: it serves /embeddings.

model.description: The embedding model, as the backend names it, such as nomic-embed-text.

min_similarity.description: How alike, by cosine similarity, a note must be to the query to be found by its meaning alone. Depends on the model; 0.5 is a start.

llm_backend.description: How the model is reached. `type` decides which other settings there are.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key, sent as x-api-key. Keys are never written in this file.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.

type.description: openai-compatible-api: any /chat/completions endpoint (llama-server, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, a hosted API).

base_url.description: Where the endpoint is, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key. Keys are never written in this file. Leave it out when the endpoint wants none.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.

model.description: The model id the endpoint serves, as its /models lists it.
